text: People directing AI coding agents may not be able to audit code, but they can say what their app must do.
Plainproof tests that requirement and gives them evidence they can inspect.
I choose the broken counter app and type the behavior I need. This is a real Meta Model API run, with generic confirmations approved only for this local app.
Muse Spark 1.3 plans structured checks, then uses the native computer tool to operate the browser. Screenshots and steps arrive as it works.
The operator works from screenshots through the native computer tool. Waiting is shown accelerated.
The model does not decide success. The counter still says ‘1 items left,’ and Python's page-text checks return FAIL.
The receipt exposes the checks the planner chose and the evidence from an independent reload. You can inspect what PASS or FAIL actually means.
Every screenshot, action and check is stored in the receipt. Checks compare literal page text.
Now I switch to the correct app. Replay is a CLI operation today: I reuse the failing receipt's executed actions and checks against this version.
Replay repeats the recorded actions with zero model calls.
The same recorded test now passes. Replay makes zero model calls and costs zero dollars in model usage. It repeats the recorded coordinates; it does not ask a model to try again.
Here is a new requirement, typed live: add one item, delete it, and leave zero items.
It passes after the item appears and is deleted. The receipt records that the marker was actually seen before it vanished.
The audit reload re-checks the final state.
This offline no-op control has the same passing final checks, but never creates the item. The marker guard makes it inconclusive, preventing a vacuous pass.
The marker guard requires this run's marker to appear at least once.
Everything shown was built for this hackathon, starting October 27, including the day-one harness. Next, I want Muse Code to fix the app from the failing receipt.
That repair loop is not built yet. Today, Plainproof provides the checks, evidence, and model-free replay.
